stem.en: A road is cut into the foot of a hillside. Months later, part of the hill slides down. How did the cut add to the risk?

text.en: It turned the hard rock of the hill into soil.

feedback.en: A cut does not change the rock itself. It changes what holds the rock up.

text.en: It stopped all rain from reaching the slope.

feedback.en: Rain still falls and soaks in. A road cut does nothing to stop it.

text.en: It removed support at the foot of the slope.

feedback.en: Yes. The rock that was removed had been holding up the ground above.

text.en: It put new weight at the very top of the hill.

feedback.en: The cut is at the foot, and it takes rock away. It adds nothing at the top.

explanation.en: A slope leans on the rock at its foot. A road cut removes some of that rock, so the ground above has less support. Heavy rain can then bring it down.

hints.en: Think about what the rock at the foot of a slope was doing.
